answer: A network can demand ambient radio presence: at random audits, each identity must report the exact set of nearby Wi-Fi and Bluetooth beacons, like a lagoon whose water only fits its own shore. A fable of a thousand clones collapses because a Sybil farm in one room shares one fingerprint, while a canyon of distance separates real devices. Each fake needs its own physically distinct radio environment, maintained around the clock — a cost that cannot be copied, split, or run in parallel.
